entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fabius Titianus was a Roman senator in the late 4th century AD, a time marked by the Constantine dynasty's ascension to power and the reorganization of the Roman Empire.

As a prominent figure in the Roman Senate, Fabius Titianus played a role in shaping the empire's administrative reforms and contributing to the development of the legal code.

His significance lies in the fact that he was one of the key figures involved in the Codification of Roman Law, a project initiated by Emperor Justinian I in the 6th century AD, which aimed to codify and standardize the Roman legal system.

Fabius Titianus's legacy can be seen in the enduring influence of Roman law on modern legal systems, particularly in the Western world.

The Roman Senate's continued relevance in modern times is a testament to the lasting impact of figures like Fabius Titianus, who helped shape the course of Roman history.
